questions.explain: SLMs have fewer parameters, so they are faster, cheaper and can run on constrained edge devices for focused tasks. A large cloud reasoning model needs connectivity and more compute; image and voice models don't classify text.

questions.stem: Which type of model converts text into numeric vectors so that you can perform semantic search over documents?
questions.explain: Embedding models output vectors that capture meaning, enabling similarity search for RAG. Chat models generate text, image models create pictures, and speech synthesis produces audio.

questions.stem: An insurance app must let customers upload a photo of a damaged car and ask, in text, 'Is the headlight broken?'. Which kind of model should you choose?
options: A multimodal model that accepts image and text input
questions.explain: The request combines an image and a text question, so a multimodal (vision-enabled) chat model is needed. Embedding, speech-to-text and text-only models can't reason over the photo.

questions.stem: You are comparing candidate models with the model leaderboards in the Microsoft Foundry portal. Which THREE categories of metrics can you compare? Select THREE.
options: Performance, such as latency and throughput
questions.explain: Foundry model leaderboards compare quality, safety, performance (latency, throughput) and cost. Training data lineage and data residency are not leaderboard metrics; residency depends on deployment type.

questions.case: Fabrikam's engineering team wants an assistant that solves complex multi-step maths and code-debugging problems. Users are willing to wait a few extra seconds if answers are more accurate. Cost per request is a secondary concern.
questions.stem: Which type of model should the team select from the model catalog?
options: A small language model optimized for lowest latency
A reasoning model that uses extra tokens to think before answering
questions.explain: Reasoning models spend additional reasoning tokens working through problems, improving accuracy on hard multi-step tasks at the cost of latency. An SLM prioritizes speed, and embedding or speech models don't solve problems.

questions.stem: For each statement about the Microsoft Foundry model catalog, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Model cards describe a model's intended uses, capabilities and limitations.
Every model in the catalog is developed by Microsoft.
A small language model generally needs less compute than a large language model.

questions.explain: Model cards document use and limitations. The catalog includes models from OpenAI, Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek, Hugging Face and others. SLMs have fewer parameters and lower compute needs.

questions.stem: You want to deploy an open model from the Hugging Face collection in the Microsoft Foundry model catalog. Which deployment option is required?
questions.explain: Hugging Face, NVIDIA NIM and custom models require managed compute, where the model runs on dedicated VMs. Global Standard and Global Batch are standard deployment types for supported Foundry Models; serverless covers pay-as-you-go catalog models.

questions.stem: Which Foundry deployment option runs the model on dedicated virtual machines and is billed by compute core hours for as long as the deployment exists, rather than by tokens?
questions.explain: Managed compute hosts the model on dedicated VMs and bills compute core hours from creation until deletion, regardless of traffic. Global Standard, Data Zone Standard and serverless API endpoints are billed by token usage.

questions.stem: For each statement about model deployment options, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A managed compute deployment continues to incur charges while it exists, even if no requests are sent.
Standard deployment in a Foundry resource supports global, data zone and regional processing.
Serverless API endpoints are billed per compute core hour.

questions.explain: Managed compute bills for uptime. Standard deployments in Foundry resources offer global, data zone and regional types. Serverless endpoints are billed by tokens, not core hours.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to start using a generative model from Microsoft Foundry in an application.
options: Deploy a model from the model catalog to the project
Test the deployment in the playground
Call the deployment's endpoint from your code by using the SDK
questions.explain: A project is needed before you can deploy a model into it. You then try the deployment in the playground and finally call its endpoint from code.

questions.case: Tailspin Toys must generate short summaries for two million archived product reviews. The job is not urgent: results any time within a day are acceptable. The priority is the lowest possible cost without affecting the live chatbot's quota.
questions.stem: Which deployment type should Tailspin use for this job?
questions.explain: Global Batch processes large files of requests asynchronously at about 50% less than Global Standard, with a 24-hour target and separate quota. Provisioned reserves paid capacity; Developer is only for evaluating fine-tuned models.

questions.case: A European bank is deploying a GPT model in Microsoft Foundry. Compliance requires that model inference is processed only within the European Union. The bank wants pay-per-token billing and as much default quota as possible within that constraint.
questions.stem: Which deployment type best meets the requirements?
questions.explain: Data Zone Standard is pay-per-token and keeps processing inside the EU data zone. Global types (Standard, Batch, Provisioned) may process requests in any Azure region, breaking the residency requirement.

questions.stem: A trading platform sends a steady, high volume of requests to a model and needs predictable latency. It is willing to pay for reserved capacity. What should you configure?
options: A provisioned deployment using provisioned throughput units (PTU)
questions.explain: Provisioned deployments reserve model capacity measured in PTUs, giving predictable throughput and latency for steady heavy workloads. Standard is shared pay-per-token; Batch is asynchronous; Developer has no SLA.

questions.stem: Which TWO deployment types are billed per token rather than for reserved capacity? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Standard types (Global Standard, Data Zone Standard, Standard) are pay-per-token. Provisioned types are billed for reserved PTU capacity.

questions.stem: A policy assistant must give consistent, focused and repeatable answers to the same question. Which configuration change helps most?
options: Raise the temperature toward the top of its range
questions.explain: Low temperature makes the model favour the most probable tokens, producing deterministic, focused output. High temperature adds randomness; presence penalty pushes new topics; removing the system prompt loses guardrails.

questions.stem: Which parameter makes the model sample only from the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a chosen threshold?
questions.explain: Top-p (nucleus sampling) restricts choices to the top tokens whose probabilities add up to p. Temperature reshapes the whole distribution; frequency penalty discourages repetition; max tokens limits length.

questions.stem: Complete the Python code so that each response is capped at 150 generated tokens.
questions.code:
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="gpt-4o-mini",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize this support ticket."}],
    ____=150
)
questions.explain: max_completion_tokens sets the upper limit on generated tokens (it replaces the older max_tokens). top_p and presence_penalty take small decimal values, and stop takes strings, not a token count.

questions.stem: For each statement about model parameters, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A positive frequency penalty reduces the chance of the model repeating the same phrases verbatim.
Presence penalty accepts values from -2.0 to 2.0.
A stop sequence forces the model to keep generating until it reaches the max token limit.

questions.explain: Frequency penalty scales with how often a token has appeared, reducing repetition. Presence and frequency penalties range from -2.0 to 2.0. A stop sequence ends generation early when that text appears.

questions.stem: A brainstorming assistant keeps circling back to the same few ideas. You want it to introduce new topics. Which parameter should you increase?
questions.explain: A positive presence penalty penalizes any token already used, pushing the model toward new topics. More max tokens only lengthens output, stop sequences end it, and a low top-p narrows choices further.

questions.stem: Complete the code so the first message sets the assistant's behaviour for the whole conversation.
questions.explain: The system role carries the system prompt that sets persona and rules. Assistant holds the model's earlier replies, and tool/function roles return tool output.

questions.stem: What most clearly distinguishes an AI agent from a basic chat completion?
options: The agent always uses a smaller model
The agent cannot be given a system prompt
The agent can reason about a goal and call tools to take actions across multiple steps
The agent answers only from its training data
questions.explain: Agents combine a model, instructions and tools so they can plan and act, for example calling APIs or searching files. Model size, prompts and training-data-only answers don't define an agent.

questions.stem: Which THREE components does every agent in Foundry Agent Service have? Select THREE.
questions.explain: An agent is defined by its model (reasoning), instructions (goals and rules) and tools (data and actions). Analyzers and custom voices belong to other Foundry Tools.

questions.case: A travel company wants an assistant that, given 'Get me to Berlin on Friday morning', checks flight availability through the airline API, books a seat, adds the trip to the traveller's calendar and emails a confirmation, without a person directing each step.
questions.stem: Which type of AI workload does this describe?
questions.explain: The assistant pursues a goal and autonomously calls several tools (APIs, calendar, email) across steps, which is agentic AI. Sentiment, OCR and speech synthesis are single-purpose perception tasks.

questions.stem: You are creating a prompt agent with the Azure AI Projects client library. Complete the code to define the agent's behaviour.
questions.code:
agent = project.agents.create_version(
    agent_name="hr-assistant",
    definition=PromptAgentDefinition(
        model="gpt-5-mini",
        ____="You are a helpful HR assistant. Answer questions about leave policy.",
    ),
)
questions.explain: A prompt agent is defined by a model plus instructions (and optional tools). The instructions parameter holds the agent's goals and rules; the other names aren't parameters of PromptAgentDefinition.

questions.stem: For each statement about generative and agentic AI, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Generative AI creates new content, such as text, code or images, in response to a prompt.
Agents in Foundry Agent Service can use tools such as file search and code interpreter.
An agent can only be created by writing code; the Foundry portal cannot create one.

questions.explain: Generative AI produces new content. Agents can use built-in tools like file search and code interpreter. Prompt agents can be created in the Foundry portal with no code.

questions.case: Contoso HR is building an agent in Foundry Agent Service. Employees will ask questions such as 'How many days of parental leave do I get?'. Answers must come from the 80-page benefits handbook PDF that HR will upload, not from the model's general knowledge.
questions.stem: Which tool should you add to the agent?
questions.explain: File search indexes uploaded documents and retrieves relevant passages to ground the agent's answers. Code interpreter runs Python for calculations; image generation and speech translation don't retrieve handbook content.

questions.stem: A call centre wants to convert its recorded customer calls into written transcripts. Which AI workload is this?
questions.explain: Turning spoken audio into text is speech recognition. Speech synthesis does the reverse, key phrase extraction analyzes existing text, and object detection works on images.

questions.stem: Which TWO scenarios are computer vision workloads? Select TWO.
options: Counting cars in frames from a traffic camera
Reading the licence plate number in a photo of a car
Detecting the language of an email
Converting a news article into spoken audio
Scoring product reviews as positive or negative
questions.explain: Counting cars (object detection) and reading plates (OCR) analyze images. Language detection and review scoring are text analysis; converting text to audio is speech synthesis.

questions.stem: An insurer needs to pull the policy number, claim date and claimed amount from thousands of scanned claim forms into a database. Which workload is this?
questions.explain: Pulling specific fields from forms into structured data is information extraction (Document Intelligence or Content Understanding). The other workloads don't produce structured fields from documents.

questions.stem: A retailer wants to know whether thousands of written product reviews are positive or negative. Which AI workload should it use?
questions.explain: Determining opinion in written text is sentiment analysis, a text analysis workload in Azure Language. Vision, speech translation and image generation don't evaluate written opinions.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if the scenario is correctly matched to its workload. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Creating marketing images from a text description is a generative AI workload.
Transcribing a podcast episode is a computer vision workload.
Finding personal data such as phone numbers in support tickets is a text analysis workload.

questions.explain: Image creation from prompts is generative AI. Transcribing audio is speech recognition, not vision. PII detection in text belongs to text analysis.

questions.case: A museum is building a mobile app for visually impaired visitors. A visitor points the phone camera at an exhibit, and the app should describe what is in the picture and read that description aloud.
questions.stem: Which combination of AI capabilities does the app need?
options: Key phrase extraction and object detection
questions.explain: Image captioning (computer vision) produces a description of the scene, and speech synthesis reads it aloud. The other pairs either analyze text, need spoken input, or create new images instead of describing one.

questions.stem: Which Azure Language feature returns the main talking points of a text, such as 'battery life' and 'delivery time'?
questions.explain: Key phrase extraction identifies the main concepts in text. Language detection identifies the language, entity linking connects entities to Wikipedia, and opinion mining attaches sentiment to aspects.

questions.stem: News articles mention 'Amazon', sometimes meaning the company and sometimes the river. You need to resolve which one is meant and return a reference URL for each. Which feature should you use?
questions.explain: Entity linking disambiguates entities by linking them to a knowledge base (Wikipedia) and returns a URL. NER only categorizes entities, key phrases list topics, and PII detection finds personal data.

questions.stem: Before storing chat transcripts for analytics, a bank must replace customer names, phone numbers and card numbers with asterisks. Which Azure Language capability should it use?
questions.explain: PII detection identifies personal information and returns redacted text. NER categorizes general entities without redaction, summarization shortens text, and classification assigns labels.

questions.stem: Which TWO are categories that prebuilt named entity recognition can assign to entities in text? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Prebuilt NER categorizes entities into types such as Person, Location, Organization and DateTime. Bounding boxes are vision outputs, neural voices are speech, and a confidence threshold is not an entity category.

questions.stem: Complete the Python code to return the main concepts discussed in each customer comment by using the Azure Language text analytics client.
questions.code:
documents = ["The checkout was slow but the support team was friendly."]
results = client.____(documents)
for doc in results:
    print(doc.key_phrases)
questions.explain: extract_key_phrases returns results with a key_phrases list. recognize_entities returns entities, analyze_sentiment returns sentiment labels, and detect_language returns the primary language.

questions.case: A pharmaceutical company receives thousands of free-text adverse-event reports. Analysts need medication names, dosages and diagnoses identified and labelled automatically so they can be filtered. No training data is available.
questions.stem: Which Azure Language capability best meets the requirement?
questions.explain: Text Analytics for health is a prebuilt feature that extracts and labels medical entities such as medications, dosages and diagnoses. Key phrases are untyped, entity linking targets Wikipedia, and language detection only identifies language.

questions.stem: A review says: 'The screen is gorgeous, but the battery dies by lunchtime.' Which overall document sentiment label is Azure Language most likely to return?
questions.explain: The review contains clearly positive and clearly negative sentences, so the document-level label is mixed. Neutral means no strong sentiment, which isn't the case here.

questions.stem: A hotel chain wants to know not just whether reviews are positive, but specifically how guests feel about aspects such as 'breakfast', 'Wi-Fi' and 'parking'. Which feature should it use?
questions.explain: Opinion mining (aspect-based sentiment) links sentiment to targets such as breakfast or parking. Key phrases list topics without sentiment, entity linking disambiguates names, and summarization shortens text.

questions.stem: Complete the Python code so that sentiment results include opinions about individual aspects of each review.
questions.code:
results = client.analyze_sentiment(
    documents,
    ____=True
)
questions.explain: Passing show_opinion_mining=True to analyze_sentiment adds aspect-level opinions (targets and assessments). show_stats returns statistics only; the other parameter names don't exist on this method.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Language features, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Extractive summarization creates new sentences that do not appear in the source text.
Language detection returns the detected language and a confidence score.
Sentiment analysis returns confidence scores for positive, neutral and negative.

questions.explain: Extractive summarization selects original sentences; abstractive writes new ones. Language detection returns the language, ISO code and confidence. Sentiment analysis includes confidence scores per label.

questions.case: A legal team needs summaries of long contracts. Because the summaries may be quoted in court filings, every sentence in the summary must appear word for word in the original contract.
questions.stem: Which approach should the team use?
questions.explain: Extractive summarization returns the most important sentences unchanged, guaranteeing verbatim text. Abstractive summarization rewrites content in new words; key phrases and opinion mining aren't summaries.

questions.stem: A global help desk receives tickets in many languages. Before routing, it wants to know each ticket's language and how upset the customer is. Which TWO Azure Language features should it use? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Language detection identifies the language for routing, and sentiment analysis measures negativity. Entity linking disambiguates names, and custom neural voice is a speech synthesis feature.

questions.stem: A conference wants live on-screen captions while speakers are presenting. Which Azure Speech capability should it use?
questions.explain: Real-time speech to text transcribes streaming audio as it is spoken, suitable for live captions. Batch transcription processes stored files asynchronously, text to speech produces audio, and pronunciation assessment scores learners.

questions.case: A manufacturer's maintenance engineers dictate repair notes on a noisy factory floor. The notes contain part codes such as 'XR-4471-B' and in-house terms that the base speech model often transcribes incorrectly.
questions.stem: What should you do to improve transcription accuracy?
options: Train a custom speech model by using recorded audio and related text from the factory
Switch from speech to text to speech translation
Use SSML to mark up the part codes
Increase the temperature of the speech model
questions.explain: Custom speech adapts recognition to your acoustic conditions and vocabulary using your own audio and text data. Speech translation translates rather than improves accuracy, SSML controls synthesis output, and temperature isn't a speech-recognition setting.

questions.stem: An insurer stores 500,000 recorded calls in Azure Blob Storage and wants them all transcribed over the next few days. Which Azure Speech option is designed for this?
questions.explain: Batch transcription asynchronously processes large volumes of stored audio via REST. Real-time transcription is for streaming audio, avatar creates video from text, and Voice Live handles live voice conversations.

questions.stem: Complete the Python code to recognize a single spoken utterance from the default microphone by using the Speech SDK.
questions.code:
import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk

speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(subscription=key, region=region)
recognizer = speechsdk.____(speech_config=speech_config)
result = recognizer.recognize_once_async().get()
print(result.text)
questions.explain: SpeechRecognizer performs speech to text and exposes recognize_once_async. SpeechSynthesizer does text to speech, TranslationRecognizer needs a SpeechTranslationConfig, and AudioDataStream handles audio output data.

questions.stem: For each statement about speech recognition, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Speech recognition converts spoken audio into text.
Batch transcription is the best choice for live captions during a video call.
Azure Speech can identify which language is being spoken in audio.

questions.explain: Speech recognition is speech to text. Batch transcription is asynchronous and unsuitable for live captions. Language identification can detect the spoken language.

questions.stem: Which markup language do you use with Azure Speech to control the pitch, speaking rate, pauses and pronunciation of synthesized speech?
questions.explain: SSML is the XML-based markup for fine-tuning text to speech output. JSON schema, YAML and KQL aren't used to shape synthesized voice characteristics.

questions.stem: Complete the Python code so the application speaks the text aloud by using a neural voice.
questions.code:
speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name = "en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural"
synthesizer = speechsdk.SpeechSynthesizer(speech_config=speech_config)
result = synthesizer.____("Your table is ready.").get()
questions.explain: speak_text_async synthesizes plain text with the configured voice (speak_ssml_async takes SSML). recognize_once_async and start_continuous_recognition are recognizer methods; translate_async isn't a synthesizer method.

questions.stem: During an international video meeting, a Spanish-speaking presenter's speech must be delivered to attendees as spoken English almost immediately. Which capability should you use?
questions.explain: Speech translation provides real-time speech-to-speech or speech-to-text translation. Batch transcription is asynchronous and doesn't translate; the other two analyze written text.

questions.case: A bank wants a phone-based voice assistant that customers can talk to naturally. It must respond with very low latency and combine speech recognition, a generative model and speech synthesis in one real-time, two-way conversation.
questions.stem: Which Azure Speech capability is designed for this?
questions.explain: Voice Live provides low-latency, real-time voice conversations between people and agents. Batch transcription is offline, pronunciation assessment scores learners, and an avatar produces talking-head video.

questions.stem: Which TWO are capabilities of text to speech in Azure Speech? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Text to speech offers prebuilt neural voices and custom voices unique to a brand. Opinion mining is text analysis, and object detection is computer vision.

questions.stem: A warehouse needs to know how many boxes are on each pallet in a photo and where each box is located. Which computer vision task should it use?
questions.explain: Object detection returns each object's label and bounding box, enabling counting and location. Classification labels the whole image, captioning describes it in a sentence, and generation creates new images.

questions.stem: Which computer vision capability extracts printed and handwritten text from a photo of a whiteboard?
questions.explain: OCR (the Read feature) extracts printed and handwritten text with its location. Classification labels images, smart crop finds an area of interest, and people detection locates people.

questions.stem: Complete the code so a vision-enabled chat model receives both a question and an image.
questions.explain: In chat completions, an image content part uses type image_url with an image_url object holding the URL or base64 data URL. input_audio is for audio, and file_search and embedding aren't content-part types.

questions.case: A quality-control line photographs every circuit board. The team needs to (1) label each photo as 'pass' or 'fail' and (2) for failed boards, show exactly where each defective component sits on the board.
questions.stem: Which TWO computer vision tasks meet the requirements? Select TWO.
questions.explain: Image classification assigns pass or fail to the whole image; object detection locates defective components with bounding boxes. Captioning only describes, while speech translation and image generation don't analyze photos.

questions.stem: For each statement about computer vision, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Image captioning returns a human-readable sentence describing an image.
Image classification returns bounding boxes for every object in an image.
A multimodal chat model can answer free-form questions about an image supplied in the prompt.

questions.explain: Captioning describes images in a sentence. Classification labels the whole image; bounding boxes come from object detection. Vision-enabled multimodal models can reason about supplied images.

questions.stem: Many image generation models create a picture by starting from random noise and refining it step by step, guided by the text prompt. What are these models called?
questions.explain: Diffusion models iteratively remove noise, guided by the prompt, to form an image. Embedding models produce vectors, RNNs are older sequence models, and decision trees are classic ML.

questions.stem: A designer has a product photo and wants a model to replace only the background with a beach scene while leaving the product untouched. What should they supply with the edit request?
options: A mask image whose transparent area marks the background
questions.explain: Image edit requests accept an optional mask where transparent pixels mark the region the model may change. Stop sequences and penalties are text-generation settings; SSML controls speech.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order for what happens when an application requests a new image from a GPT-image deployment in Microsoft Foundry.
options: The application sends a text prompt to the image generation endpoint
Content filters check the generated image
The image is returned to the application as base64 data
questions.explain: Both the prompt and the output pass through content filtering. The prompt is checked before generation and the image is checked afterwards, before base64 image data is returned.

questions.stem: In Azure Content Understanding, which component defines the extraction settings, the field schema and the model deployments that are applied to every incoming file?
questions.explain: An analyzer is Content Understanding's reusable configuration, holding the field schema and settings. Deployment types relate to model hosting, neural voices to speech, and system prompts to chat models.

questions.stem: Which THREE content types (modalities) can Azure Content Understanding analyze? Select THREE.
questions.explain: Content Understanding supports documents, images, audio and video. Market feeds and database schemas aren't supported modalities.

questions.case: A contact centre uses Azure Content Understanding on recorded calls. For each call, it wants a field named CallSummary containing a short paragraph describing what the customer wanted and how the call ended. The words don't need to appear verbatim in the recording.
questions.stem: Which field method should CallSummary use?
questions.explain: Generate creates free-form values such as summaries. Extract copies values as they appear (documents only), classify picks from predefined categories, and redact is not a Content Understanding field method.

questions.stem: For each statement about Azure Content Understanding, select Yes if the statement is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A classify field chooses a value from a predefined set of categories.
Confidence scores can be used to decide which results need human review.
Content Understanding can return output only as plain text, not as structured JSON.

questions.explain: Classify picks from defined categories. Confidence scores (0 to 1) support straight-through processing or review. Output can be Markdown or structured JSON that matches your schema.

questions.case: An HR department receives the same type of tax statement from 300 different employers. Every statement contains the same information (employee name, employer ID, total wages), but each employer uses a different layout. The prebuilt models don't cover this form.
questions.stem: Which Document Intelligence model type should you train?
questions.explain: A custom neural model handles varied layouts containing the same information with one model. Custom template suits a single fixed layout; Read and Layout extract text and structure but not your named fields.

questions.stem: An accounts-payable team wants to capture the vendor name, invoice date and total from supplier invoices with no model training. What should it use?
options: The Document Intelligence prebuilt invoice model
questions.explain: The prebuilt invoice model returns invoice fields such as vendor, date and total without training. The other options don't extract invoice fields.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to automate processing of supplier invoices with an information extraction service.
options: Submit each file to the extraction model
Receive structured fields with confidence scores
Send low-confidence fields for human review
Write the approved values to the finance system
questions.explain: Files are collected and submitted for analysis, the service returns fields with confidence scores, low-confidence values are reviewed by a person, and approved data is written to the downstream system.

questions.stem: You want the rule 'Only answer questions about our return policy' to apply to every turn of a chat. Where should you put it?
questions.explain: The system prompt sets role and rules for the whole conversation. User prompts change every turn, stop sequences only end generation, and assistant messages are the model's earlier replies, not instructions.

questions.stem: For each statement about prompts, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The user prompt is normally written by the developer and stays the same for every request.
A system prompt can tell the model which output format to use, such as JSON.
Adding a system prompt permanently retrains the deployed model.

questions.explain: The user prompt comes from the end user and changes each turn. System prompts can define output format. Prompts only condition the current request; they never change model weights.

questions.case: A tutoring app uses a deployed model. The developer configures it to act as a patient maths tutor, never reveal final answers, and keep replies under three sentences. A student then types a homework problem into the app.
questions.stem: Which text is the user prompt?
options: You are a patient maths tutor who explains step by step.
Never reveal the final answer; ask a guiding question instead.
Keep every reply under three sentences.
questions.explain: The student's homework problem is the user prompt. The persona, the 'never reveal' rule and the length limit are developer-set rules that belong in the system prompt.

questions.stem: Which TWO items typically belong in a system prompt? Select TWO.
options: The end user's specific question about their order
What to do when the answer is unknown
The base64 audio of the user's voice
questions.explain: System prompts define persona, scope, tone and fallback behaviour such as 'say you don't know'. The user's question and audio are user input; a subscription ID isn't prompt content.

questions.stem: A chat assistant sometimes invents answers when it does not know them. Which system prompt change best addresses this?
options: Tell the model to say 'I don't know' when the answer isn't in the provided information
Move all instructions into the user prompt
questions.explain: Giving the model an explicit 'out' reduces fabricated answers. Higher temperature increases randomness, moving instructions doesn't help, and more output tokens only allow longer answers.

questions.stem: In a Chat Completions messages list, which role carries the system prompt?
questions.explain: The system role holds developer instructions, usually as the first message. user holds the end user's input, assistant holds model replies, and tool holds tool results.

questions.case: Contoso deploys a customer service chatbot whose system prompt is only 'You are a helpful assistant.' Testers find it happily answers cooking and sports questions, which management wants it to decline. The bot should only discuss Contoso orders.
questions.stem: What should you do?
options: Add to the system prompt: 'Only answer questions about Contoso orders and politely decline other topics.'
Ask every user to start messages with 'Contoso:'
Redeploy the model with the Global Batch deployment type
questions.explain: Scope restrictions belong in the system prompt. Relying on users is unreliable, top-p only changes randomness, and Global Batch is an asynchronous deployment type that doesn't change behaviour.

questions.stem: You include two worked input/output examples in a prompt before the real request. What is this technique called?
questions.explain: Few-shot prompting supplies a few examples in the prompt. Zero-shot uses none, chain-of-thought asks for step-by-step reasoning, and fine-tuning retrains the model on data.

questions.stem: You paste your company's leave policy into the prompt and tell the model to answer only from that text. Which technique is this?
options: Grounding the prompt with supplied context
questions.explain: Supplying source content and limiting answers to it is grounding. Few-shot uses examples, prompt shields detect jailbreak attacks, and the context window is a model limit, not a technique.

questions.stem: Which TWO prompt techniques help reduce hallucinations? Select TWO.
options: Supply source content and instruct the model to answer only from it
Tell the model to reply 'not found' when the source lacks the answer
questions.explain: Grounding plus an explicit fallback keeps answers tied to facts. Maximum temperature makes output more random, removing the system prompt removes guidance, and frequency penalty only reduces repetition.

questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Few-shot examples in a prompt permanently change the model's weights.
Asking a model to work through a problem step by step is chain-of-thought prompting.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) retrieves relevant data and adds it to the prompt to ground the response.

questions.explain: Examples only condition the current request; weights change only through training. Step-by-step reasoning prompts are chain of thought. RAG retrieves data and injects it into the prompt.

questions.stem: Your app passes model output to a JSON parser, but the model often adds friendly sentences around the data. What is the most direct prompt-level fix?
options: Specify the exact JSON structure in the system prompt and ask for JSON only
questions.explain: Stating the required output format (and that nothing else should be returned) is the output-format technique. Token limits and penalties don't control structure, and zero-shot removes helpful examples.

questions.stem: A model produces a fluent, confident answer that is factually false. What is this called?
questions.explain: A hallucination is confident output not supported by facts. Grounding is the mitigation, tokenization splits text into tokens, and throttling is rate limiting.

questions.case: An analyst's prompt starts with 'Return exactly five bullet points', followed by a 6,000-word report to summarise. The model reads the whole report but usually returns long paragraphs instead of bullets. The analyst wants to keep the same model and settings.
questions.stem: Based on Microsoft prompt engineering guidance, what should the analyst try first?
options: Send the report to a second deployment
Repeat the key format instruction at the end of the prompt, after the report
questions.explain: Models show recency bias: instructions at the end of a long prompt carry more weight, so repeating the format instruction there helps. The other options add randomness or don't address instruction placement.

questions.stem: In the Foundry portal, where do you browse and compare models from Microsoft, OpenAI, Meta, Mistral and others before deploying one?
questions.explain: The model catalog lists models with model cards and benchmarks and lets you deploy them. The agent playground tests agents, Azure Marketplace sells third-party products, and the Language playground tests Azure Language.

questions.stem: Which deployment type is the default, is billed per token, may process data in any Azure region, and offers the highest default quota?
questions.explain: Global Standard is the default pay-per-token type with global processing. Standard keeps processing in the geography, Data Zone Standard in a data zone, and Provisioned uses reserved PTUs.

questions.case: A German insurer is deploying a chat model in Foundry. Compliance requires that prompts and responses are processed only within the EU. The team expects bursty traffic, wants high quota and wants to pay only for tokens used rather than reserving capacity.
questions.stem: Which deployment type should they choose?
questions.explain: Data Zone Standard keeps processing in the EU data zone with pay-per-token billing and high quotas. Global Standard and Global Batch can process anywhere; Developer is only for evaluating fine-tuned models.

questions.case: A publisher wants to summarise 200,000 archived articles. Results are needed within about a day, nobody is waiting interactively, and the priority is the lowest cost. Normal interactive traffic on the same model must not be disrupted.
questions.stem: Which deployment type best fits?
questions.explain: Global Batch is asynchronous with a 24-hour target turnaround, about 50% cheaper, and uses separate enqueued quota. Provisioned reserves costly capacity, Standard is interactive pay-per-token, Developer is for fine-tuned evaluation.

questions.stem: For each statement about model deployments, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Provisioned deployments are billed by reserved provisioned throughput units (PTUs) rather than per token.
Exceeding a deployment's tokens-per-minute (TPM) limit can cause rate-limit errors.
Every model in the catalog supports every deployment type in every region.

questions.explain: Provisioned types reserve PTUs. TPM limits throttle requests when exceeded. Availability of deployment types varies by model and region.

questions.stem: An app frequently receives rate-limit errors from a deployment. Which TWO changes in the app can reduce them? Select TWO.
options: Lower the max output tokens per request
Reduce the number of concurrent requests
Move the system prompt into the user prompt
questions.explain: Larger max token settings and more concurrent calls consume more TPM. Temperature doesn't affect quota, moving instructions changes nothing, and extra examples add tokens, making throttling worse.

questions.stem: You are starting from an Azure subscription. Put the steps in order to begin chatting with a new model in the Foundry portal.
options: Create or open a Foundry project
Open the model catalog and select a model
Select Deploy and choose the deployment settings
questions.explain: Models are deployed inside a project, so the project comes first. You choose the model from the catalog, deploy it to get an endpoint, then interact with it in the playground.

questions.case: A research team wants to run an open-source model from the catalog's Hugging Face collection. They need dedicated GPU capacity for it and accept hourly billing per accelerator. They don't want to manage virtual machines or serving runtimes themselves.
questions.stem: Which deployment option fits?
questions.explain: Managed compute runs open-source and custom models on dedicated GPUs billed hourly, with Foundry managing the runtime. Serverless API types are pay-per-token for Foundry Models; Developer is for fine-tuned evaluation.

questions.stem: Which parameter makes a model's output more random and creative when you increase it?
questions.explain: Higher temperature flattens token probabilities, giving more varied output. Max output tokens limits length, a stop sequence ends output, and frequency penalty reduces repetition.

questions.stem: A legal team wants generated contract clauses to be focused and consistent between runs. Which playground setting should they use?
options: Remove the max output tokens limit
questions.explain: Low temperature gives focused, repeatable output, which suits legal text. High temperature adds creativity, presence penalty pushes new topics, and output length doesn't affect consistency.

questions.stem: For each statement about model parameters, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Microsoft recommends adjusting temperature or top-p, but not both at the same time.
Max output tokens limits the length of the model's response.
A stop sequence forces the model to keep generating until it reaches the max token limit.

questions.explain: Temperature and top-p both control randomness, so change one. Max output tokens caps length. A stop sequence does the opposite: it makes generation stop when that text appears.

questions.stem: A model keeps repeating the same phrases. Which parameter penalises tokens in proportion to how often they have already appeared?
questions.explain: Frequency penalty scales with how often a token has appeared, cutting repetition. Presence penalty applies once a token has appeared at all, encouraging new topics; top-p and temperature control randomness.

questions.stem: Which THREE can you configure directly in the Foundry model playground? Select THREE.
options: The Azure region of the Foundry resource
questions.explain: The playground exposes instructions and generation parameters such as temperature and max tokens. Training data is fixed by the model provider, and the region is set when the resource is created.

questions.stem: Which list shows the harm categories that Foundry guardrails (content filters) classify for model input and output?
questions.explain: Foundry content risk controls, based on Azure AI Content Safety, classify hate, sexual, violence and self-harm content with severity levels. The other lists aren't the content filter categories.

questions.stem: You have tuned prompts and parameters in the playground and want starter Python code that reproduces them. What is the quickest option?
options: Export the deployment as an ARM template
Download the model weights from the catalog
Use the playground's code view to copy the generated sample code
questions.explain: The playground generates sample code that calls your deployment with the same prompts and settings. ARM templates deploy infrastructure, hosted models' weights aren't downloadable for this, and the Language playground is a different service.

questions.case: A support chatbot's answers often stop mid-sentence. Logs show each response ends exactly when the output token count hits the configured limit. Answer accuracy is otherwise fine and no stop sequences are configured.
questions.stem: What should you change?
options: Increase the max output tokens setting
questions.explain: Responses are truncated by the max output tokens cap, so raise it (or ask for shorter answers). Temperature and presence penalty change wording, and a stop sequence would end output even sooner.

questions.stem: Which Python package is the Foundry SDK client library that provides the AIProjectClient class?
questions.explain: azure-ai-projects (the Azure AI Projects client library) provides AIProjectClient. azure-ai-textanalytics is for Azure Language, azure-cognitiveservices-speech is the Speech SDK, and azure-mgmt-resource manages Azure resources.

questions.stem: Complete the code to create a Foundry project client that authenticates with Microsoft Entra ID.
questions.code:
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

project = AIProjectClient(
    endpoint=project_endpoint,
    credential=____,
)
questions.explain: DefaultAzureCredential() obtains an Entra ID token (az login locally, managed identity in Azure). AzureKeyCredential is key-based, a raw environment string isn't a credential object, and SpeechConfig belongs to the Speech SDK.

questions.stem: Complete the code so the app gets an OpenAI-compatible client from the Foundry project and calls the model deployment.
questions.code:
project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=project_endpoint, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
openai = project.____()
response = openai.responses.create(model="support-gpt", input=user_text)
print(response.output_text)
questions.explain: get_openai_client() returns an OpenAI-compatible client bound to the project endpoint for the Responses API. The other method names don't return a client that exposes responses.create.

questions.stem: You deployed gpt-4.1-mini with the deployment name 'faq-bot'. What value should you pass as the model argument to responses.create?
questions.explain: Calls target a deployment, so model takes the deployment name, which can differ from the underlying model name. The project and resource group names identify containers, not the deployment.

questions.stem: Which URL format is a Foundry project endpoint used with AIProjectClient?
questions.explain: The project endpoint is the Foundry resource host plus /api/projects/<project-name>. portal.azure.com and ai.azure.com are web portals, and the tts host is a Speech endpoint.

questions.case: A developer's Python chat client uses AIProjectClient with DefaultAzureCredential. It works on her laptop after she runs az login. When deployed to Azure App Service with a system-assigned managed identity, every call fails with an authorisation (403) error. The endpoint is correct.
questions.stem: What is the most likely fix?
options: Replace DefaultAzureCredential with the API key string
Assign the App Service managed identity the Foundry User role on the Foundry project
Change the deployment type to Global Standard
questions.explain: The managed identity authenticates but lacks permission; granting Foundry User (formerly Azure AI User) or higher fixes it. AIProjectClient expects a token credential, deployment type doesn't affect authorisation, and textanalytics is unrelated.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to build a minimal Foundry SDK chat client in Python.
options: Create an AIProjectClient with the project endpoint and DefaultAzureCredential
Call get_openai_client() on the project client
Call responses.create with the deployment name and the user's input
questions.explain: Packages first, then the project client, then the OpenAI-compatible client, then the call, and finally display the generated text from output_text.

questions.stem: Complete the Responses API call so the second turn keeps the context of the first.
questions.code:
first = client.responses.create(model="chat-dep", input="Who was Ada Lovelace?")
second = client.responses.create(
    model="chat-dep",
    ____=first.id,
    input="Tell me more about her work with Charles Babbage.",
)
questions.explain: previous_response_id chains a response to the prior one so only the new input is sent. thread_id is the classic Agents API concept, and the other names aren't Responses API parameters.

questions.stem: Which authentication method does Microsoft recommend for an app running in Azure that calls a Foundry model, because it avoids storing secrets?
options: Microsoft Entra ID with a managed identity
An API key hard-coded in the source
An API key in a public configuration file
questions.explain: Entra ID with a managed identity uses tokens with no long-lived secret. Hard-coded or public keys are insecure, and Foundry endpoints don't allow anonymous calls.

questions.stem: For each statement about multi-turn chat, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: With Chat Completions, a model automatically remembers earlier requests even if you don't resend them.
Resending the full message history on every turn increases the number of tokens per request.
If the prompt, history and output exceed the model's context window, the request can fail or history must be trimmed.

questions.explain: Models are stateless, so history must be resent or chained. Growing history adds tokens each turn, and everything must fit in the context window.

questions.stem: Complete the code that creates an OpenAI client for key-based access to a Foundry (Azure OpenAI) v1 endpoint.
questions.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    base_url="https://contoso-ai.openai.azure.com/openai/v1/",
    ____=os.getenv("API_KEY"),
)
questions.explain: The OpenAI client takes base_url and api_key. credential is used by Azure SDK clients, subscription by the Speech SDK, and the OpenAI client uses base_url rather than endpoint.

questions.stem: What are tokens in the context of large language models?
options: API keys used to authenticate requests
Small units of text, such as words or word pieces, that a model reads and generates
Credits purchased in advance to pay for Azure
Images used to verify a user is human
questions.explain: Tokens are the text units a model processes; they drive cost, TPM limits and context size. Despite the name, they aren't keys, prepaid credits or CAPTCHA images.

questions.stem: A Python chat client uses an endpoint and API key. Which TWO practices keep the key secure? Select TWO.
options: Store the key in a .env file excluded from source control and load it with load_dotenv()
Commit the key to the Git repository for teammates
Store the key in Azure Key Vault and read it at runtime
Paste the key into the system prompt
Print the key in application logs for troubleshooting
questions.explain: Keep keys out of code: environment/.env files (not committed) or Key Vault. Committing, logging or sending the key to the model exposes it.

questions.case: A chat app sends each user message to responses.create with only input=user_text. Users complain that when they ask 'What about the second one?', the model has no idea what they were talking about. The team wants the service to manage the history rather than resending it themselves.
questions.stem: What should they change?
options: Raise the temperature so the model guesses context
Switch the deployment to Provisioned throughput
Pass previous_response_id (or a conversation) on each call
questions.explain: Each call is independent; chaining with previous_response_id or a stored conversation lets the service supply prior context. Token limits, temperature and deployment type don't add memory.

questions.stem: Which THREE components define a prompt agent in Foundry Agent Service? Select THREE.
questions.explain: A prompt agent is configuration only: model, instructions and tools. Foundry runs it, so there are no VMs to manage; a container image you build is what a hosted agent uses.

questions.stem: In Foundry Agent Service, what are an agent's instructions?
options: The list of tools the agent can call
The deployment type of its model
The agent's system prompt defining role, behaviour, style and constraints
questions.explain: Instructions play the role of the system prompt for the agent. Tools are configured separately, the deployment type belongs to the model deployment, and conversation logs are stored state.

questions.stem: You configured instructions and tools in the model playground and want to keep this setup as a reusable agent. What should you do?
options: Change the deployment type to Provisioned
questions.explain: Save as agent stores the model, instructions and tools as an agent you can test and call. New chat only clears history, deployment type affects capacity, and a transcript isn't an agent definition.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order to create and test a single agent in the Foundry portal.
options: Select a deployed model for the agent
Chat with it in the agent playground
questions.explain: Choose the model, define behaviour with instructions, add tools, save (creating a version), then test and refine in the playground.

questions.stem: For each statement about Foundry agents, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A prompt agent requires you to write and host your own container code.
Saving changes to an agent creates a new version that you can compare or roll back.
Selecting New chat in the agent playground starts a conversation without the previous turns' context.

questions.explain: Prompt agents are configuration only; hosted agents use your container code. Saves create versions. New chat resets context, which is useful when retesting changed instructions.

questions.case: A team built a 'computing-historian' agent whose instructions say to answer only computing-history questions. During testing it still answers 'What's the capital of Spain?'. The model and tools are appropriate and no errors occur.
questions.stem: What should the team do first?
options: Strengthen the instructions to explicitly decline unrelated topics, save, and retest in a new chat
questions.explain: Behaviour is controlled by the instructions, so make the scope rule explicit, save, and retest with fresh context. A new tool, hosted agent or more quota doesn't change topic handling.

questions.stem: An agent must answer questions using 30 internal product manuals that you upload. Which tool should you add?
questions.explain: File search indexes uploaded documents in a vector store and retrieves relevant passages with citations. Web search uses the public internet, code interpreter runs Python, and image generation creates images.

questions.stem: Users upload CSV sales files and ask the agent to calculate totals and draw a chart. Which tool enables this?
questions.explain: Code interpreter writes and runs Python in a sandbox, so it can compute and plot data. File search retrieves text, web search finds public pages, and Azure AI Search queries an existing index.

questions.stem: You describe a get_order_status function to an agent. When the agent decides to use it, what happens?
options: Foundry automatically writes the function code
The web search tool looks up the order status
The model executes the function inside its own weights
Your application runs the function and returns the result to the agent
questions.explain: With function calling the agent returns which function to call and with what arguments; your app executes it and passes the output back. Foundry doesn't write the code, and web search can't see private orders.

questions.case: A travel agency builds a single agent. It must (1) answer questions from its own brochure PDFs and (2) report today's flight disruption news from public websites, with citations. No custom code should be written.
questions.stem: Which TWO tools should be added? Select TWO.
questions.explain: File search grounds on the uploaded brochures and web search retrieves current public news with citations. Function calling needs your own code, code interpreter is for computation, and computer use drives UIs.

questions.stem: For each statement about agent tools, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting agents to tools and data sources.
The web search tool can search documents you uploaded to the agent's vector store.
An OpenAPI tool lets an agent call a REST API described by an OpenAPI specification.

questions.explain: MCP standardises tool connections. Uploaded documents are searched by file search, not web search. OpenAPI tools call REST APIs from their specification.

questions.stem: Your company already maintains an Azure AI Search index of policy documents. Which tool lets an agent ground answers on that existing index?
questions.explain: The Azure AI Search tool connects an agent to an existing index. File search builds its own vector store from uploaded files, code interpreter runs code, and browser automation performs web tasks.

questions.stem: Complete the Foundry SDK code that creates a prompt agent.
questions.code:
agent = project.agents.create_version(
    agent_name="hr-helper",
    definition=____(
        model="gpt-4.1-mini",
        instructions="Answer HR policy questions concisely.",
    ),
)
questions.explain: PromptAgentDefinition holds the model, instructions and tools for a prompt agent passed to create_version. The other classes belong to the Speech SDK, Azure Language SDK and key authentication.

questions.stem: Complete the code so both questions are sent to the agent in the same multi-turn conversation.
questions.code:
openai = project.get_openai_client(agent_name="hr-helper")
conv = openai.conversations.create()
r1 = openai.responses.create(conversation=conv.id, input="How many leave days do I get?")
r2 = openai.responses.create(____, input="Can I carry them over?")
questions.explain: Reusing conversation=conv.id keeps both turns in the same stored conversation. A model name alone starts fresh, thread is a classic concept not used here, and streaming doesn't add context.

questions.stem: In the current Foundry Agent Service API, which object replaces the classic 'thread' for storing a multi-turn exchange?
questions.explain: Threads became conversations, which store items such as messages and tool calls. Runs became responses, assistants became agent versions, and a deployment hosts a model.

questions.stem: Put the steps in order for a Python client to chat with an existing Foundry agent.
options: Create an AIProjectClient with the project endpoint and credential
Get an OpenAI client for the agent from the project client
Call responses.create with the conversation and user input
questions.explain: Connect to the project, get the OpenAI-compatible client bound to the agent, create a conversation for state, send input, then read the generated text.

questions.case: A developer is migrating an app written for the classic Agents API (threads, messages, runs polled until complete) to azure-ai-projects 2.x and the Responses API.
questions.stem: For each statement, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: In the new API, a response is returned without having to poll a run until it completes.
Agents are created with the project client, while conversations and responses use the OpenAI client from get_openai_client().
Existing classic threads are automatically converted into new conversations by the SDK upgrade.

questions.explain: Responses replace polled runs. Agent creation uses AIProjectClient; conversations and responses use the OpenAI client. Migration moves code, not stored thread state; new conversations start fresh.

questions.stem: Which text analysis feature returns the ISO 639-1 code (such as 'es') and a confidence score for a document?
questions.explain: Language detection identifies the primary language with its ISO 639-1 code and confidence. Key phrases list topics, entity linking connects entities to a knowledge base, and sentiment scores opinion.

questions.stem: A hospital must mask patients' names, phone numbers and addresses in free-text notes before analysts see them. Which feature should it use?
questions.explain: PII detection finds personal (and health) data and returns redacted text. NER categorises entities but doesn't redact, key phrases list topics, and summaries can still contain personal data.

questions.stem: A news app must tell whether 'Mercury' in an article means the planet or the chemical element, and attach a reference link. Which feature does this?
questions.explain: Entity linking disambiguates entities and links them to a knowledge base such as Wikipedia. NER only categorises the entity, opinion mining handles sentiment on aspects, and language detection identifies language.

questions.stem: A hotel review says 'The room was spotless but the breakfast was cold.' You need to know that 'room' was positive and 'breakfast' negative. Which feature provides this?
questions.explain: Opinion mining (aspect-based sentiment) links each target, such as room or breakfast, to its opinion and sentiment. Document sentiment would likely return mixed, and key phrases or entity linking don't assign sentiment.

questions.stem: You want to automatically generate tags listing the main talking points of each support article. Which feature fits best?
questions.explain: Key phrase extraction returns the main concepts in text, ideal for tags and indexing. PII detection finds personal data, language detection identifies language, and speech synthesis produces audio.

questions.case: A bank processes 50,000 customer emails a day in an automated pipeline. Each email must be tagged with a language code and have personal data masked, and downstream systems need the same structured output format for every email. Developers don't want results that vary with prompt wording.
questions.stem: Which approach should they use?
options: Azure Language in Foundry Tools analyzers
A general-purpose chat model in the chat playground
A Global Batch deployment of an image model
questions.explain: Azure Language analyzers return structured, consistent results, which suits automated pipelines. A general-purpose model's output varies with phrasing, a voice agent is for speech, and an image model is irrelevant.

questions.stem: For each statement about text analysis options in Foundry, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: A general-purpose LLM can summarise text and classify sentiment from a natural language prompt.
A general-purpose LLM is guaranteed to return identical wording each time for the same prompt.
You can ask a general-purpose model follow-up questions about its analysis in the same chat.

questions.explain: LLMs handle many text tasks via prompts and support conversational follow-ups, but generation is probabilistic, so wording can vary between calls.

questions.stem: Named entity recognition should return categories for which TWO items in 'Maria met Contoso in Paris on 3 May'? Select TWO.
questions.explain: NER categorises entities such as people, organisations, locations and dates. It doesn't tag parts of speech like verbs or prepositions, and sentiment comes from sentiment analysis.

questions.stem: Complete the code to create an Azure Language client that authenticates with a key.
questions.code:
from azure.core.credentials import AzureKeyCredential
from azure.ai.textanalytics import TextAnalyticsClient

client = ____(endpoint=endpoint, credential=AzureKeyCredential(key))
questions.explain: TextAnalyticsClient is the Azure Language client and takes endpoint plus credential. AIProjectClient is for Foundry projects, SpeechRecognizer is the Speech SDK, and OpenAI takes base_url and api_key.

questions.stem: Complete the code to print the masked version of a document after PII detection.
questions.code:
result = client.recognize_pii_entities([text])[0]
print("Masked:", result.____)
questions.explain: PII results expose redacted_text plus an entities list. primary_language belongs to language detection, key_phrases to key phrase extraction, and sentiment to sentiment analysis results.

questions.stem: Complete the code to print the detected language's name for a document.
questions.code:
result = client.detect_language([text])[0]
print(result.____.name)
questions.explain: detect_language results have primary_language with name, iso6391_name and confidence_score. entities and redacted_text belong to PII results, and confidence_scores belongs to sentiment results.

questions.stem: For each statement about the azure-ai-textanalytics client library, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: Methods such as detect_language accept a list of documents and return one result per document.
Each PII entity result includes its text, category and confidence score.
The library is installed with pip install azure-cognitiveservices-speech.

questions.explain: Text Analytics methods process document lists, and PII entities expose text, category and confidence_score. The package is azure-ai-textanalytics; azure-cognitiveservices-speech is the Speech SDK.

questions.case: A support team has a Foundry agent that triages tickets. They want it to detect each ticket's language and redact PII using Azure Language, without writing code that calls the Language REST API or manages its tokens. They already have a Foundry resource.
questions.stem: What should they do?
options: Create a separate Azure Language resource and call it from a function tool
Add the Azure Language in Foundry Tools (MCP) tool to the agent and connect it with the Foundry resource name
Add the code interpreter tool and install azure-ai-textanalytics in it
Enable Voice mode on the agent
questions.explain: The Azure Language MCP server exposes Language features as agent tools; you connect it with your Foundry resource name, which already includes Language. The other options require extra code or are unrelated.

questions.stem: In Model Context Protocol (MCP), what role does an AI agent that uses an external tool play?
questions.explain: The agent (or its host app) is the MCP client that sends requests; the service exposing tools, such as the Azure Language MCP server, is the MCP server.

questions.stem: Which TWO TextAnalyticsClient methods would you call to find the main topics of reviews and classify how customers feel? Select TWO.
questions.explain: extract_key_phrases returns topics and analyze_sentiment returns positive/negative/neutral/mixed labels. PII and language detection answer different questions, and speak_text_async is a Speech SDK method.

questions.stem: What makes a model 'multimodal'?
options: It is deployed in more than one region
It accepts or produces more than one type of data, such as text, audio and images
It has more than one deployment name
It uses both temperature and top-p
questions.explain: Multimodal refers to modalities: text, audio, images and so on. Regions, deployment names and sampling parameters have nothing to do with it.

questions.stem: Complete the message content part that sends a recorded WAV question to an audio-capable chat model.
questions.code:
content = [
    {"type": "text", "text": "Answer the question in this recording."},
    {"type": "____", "input_audio": {"data": encoded_wav, "format": "wav"}},
]
questions.explain: Audio input uses a content part of type input_audio with base64 data and its format. image_url sends images, audio_url isn't the defined part type, and file_search is an agent tool.

questions.stem: For each statement about sending spoken prompts to an audio-capable model, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: The audio file is base64-encoded before being placed in the request.
Setting modalities to include 'audio' lets the model return a spoken response.
You must first run the audio through a separate speech-to-text service before an audio-native model can use it.

questions.explain: Audio bytes are base64-encoded in input_audio. Requesting the audio modality (with a voice and format) returns speech. Audio-native models accept audio directly, so no separate STT step is required.

questions.stem: An audio chat completion returns both text and speech. Where is the text version of the spoken reply found?
questions.explain: message.audio.transcript holds the text and message.audio.data holds base64 audio to decode and play. redacted_text is a PII result and translations is a speech translation result.

questions.case: A retailer is building a browser-based shopping assistant. Customers speak into their laptop microphone and expect the assistant to reply aloud almost instantly, with natural back-and-forth conversation. The team plans to use a gpt-realtime model.
questions.stem: Which connection method for the Realtime API is recommended for this client-side scenario?
options: Batch transcription with a SAS URI
questions.explain: WebRTC is recommended for low-latency audio in browser and mobile clients. SIP is for telephony, WebSocket suits server-to-server, and batch options are asynchronous and far too slow.

questions.stem: Which model family is designed for low-latency 'speech in, speech out' conversations through the Realtime API?
questions.explain: gpt-realtime models stream audio in and out with low latency. Embedding models produce vectors, gpt-image generates images, and a text-only model can't hear audio.

questions.case: A developer records a user's spoken question as question.wav and wants a deployed gpt-4o-audio-preview model to answer it aloud, saving the reply as answer.wav.
questions.stem: Which TWO request settings are needed? Select TWO.
options: A user content part of type input_audio containing the base64 WAV data
modalities set to include both text and audio, with an audio voice and format
questions.explain: The audio goes in as an input_audio part, and requesting the audio modality with voice and format returns spoken output. Translation config, opinion mining and stop sequences are unrelated.

questions.stem: Which Azure Speech capability provides a fully managed speech-to-speech service that combines speech recognition, a generative model and speech synthesis for voice agents?
questions.explain: Voice Live orchestrates STT, the generative model and TTS in one low-latency service. Batch transcription processes stored files, custom neural voice creates a voice, and speech translation translates speech.

questions.stem: In the Foundry portal you have a working text agent and want users to talk to it by microphone. Which setting do you enable?
questions.explain: Voice mode adds Voice Live speech input and output to the agent definition. Code interpreter runs Python, deployment type controls capacity, and PII redaction is a Language feature.

questions.stem: Which THREE conversational features does Voice Live provide? Select THREE.
options: Automatic fine-tuning of the generative model
questions.explain: Voice Live includes noise suppression, echo cancellation, robust interruption handling and end-of-turn detection. It doesn't fine-tune models or redact document PII.

questions.stem: Put the stages of a voice agent's turn in order.
options: Capture the user's speech from the microphone
Convert the reply text to speech
Play the audio through the speaker
questions.explain: A speech-to-speech pipeline captures audio, recognises it, reasons with the model, synthesises the reply, then plays it. Voice Live manages all of these stages as one service.

questions.case: A city council wants a kiosk voice assistant in a noisy lobby. Residents often pause mid-sentence or interrupt the assistant while it's speaking. The small dev team doesn't want to wire together separate speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech services or manage the underlying models.
questions.stem: Which solution best fits?
options: Batch transcription feeding a chat model, then Text to Speech
Azure Language in Foundry Tools with opinion mining
A Global Batch deployment of gpt-4.1
A Foundry agent with Voice mode (Voice Live)
questions.explain: Voice Live handles noise suppression, interruptions and end-of-turn detection as a managed service. A hand-built batch chain is slow and complex, Language is text-only, and Global Batch is asynchronous.

questions.stem: For each statement about Voice Live, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: You choose a generative model, such as a GPT-Realtime or GPT-4.1 model, for Voice Live to use.
You must deploy and host the Voice Live acoustic models on your own GPUs.
Voice Live uses WebSocket events designed to be compatible with the Azure OpenAI Realtime API.

questions.explain: You pick the generative model, but Voice Live is fully managed, so you don't deploy its models. It uses WebSocket events compatible with the Realtime API.

questions.stem: Which pip package provides the Azure Speech SDK for Python?
questions.explain: azure-cognitiveservices-speech is the Speech SDK (SpeechRecognizer, SpeechSynthesizer). azure-ai-voicelive is for Voice Live sessions, textanalytics is Azure Language, and azure-ai-projects is the Foundry SDK.

questions.stem: Complete the code so the recognizer transcribes a voicemail file instead of the microphone.
questions.code:
speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(subscription=key, endpoint=endpoint)
audio_config = speechsdk.audio.AudioConfig(____)
recognizer = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(speech_config=speech_config, audio_config=audio_config)
result = recognizer.recognize_once_async().get()
questions.explain: AudioConfig(filename=...) reads audio from a file. use_default_microphone captures live input, use_default_speaker belongs to AudioOutputConfig for playback, and voice_name isn't an AudioConfig parameter.

questions.stem: Complete the check that confirms speech was successfully transcribed.
questions.explain: RecognizedSpeech signals a successful transcription. SynthesizingAudioCompleted is for text-to-speech, TranslatedSpeech for translation, and NoMatch means no speech could be recognised.

questions.case: An app uses recognize_once_async() to transcribe hour-long board meetings streamed from a microphone. Only the first sentence or so of each meeting appears in the transcript.
questions.stem: What should the developer change?
options: Use start_continuous_recognition() with recognized event handlers
questions.explain: recognize_once_async handles a single utterance (about 30 seconds or until silence). Long audio needs continuous recognition with event handlers. The other options relate to speech synthesis.

questions.stem: Complete the code so spoken English is translated into French text.
questions.code:
config = speechsdk.translation.SpeechTranslationConfig(subscription=key, endpoint=endpoint)
config.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"
config.____("fr")
recognizer = speechsdk.translation.TranslationRecognizer(translation_config=config, audio_config=audio_config)
questions.explain: add_target_language adds a translation target such as 'fr'; results appear in result.translations['fr']. speech_synthesis_language is a TTS setting, and the others aren't SpeechTranslationConfig methods.

questions.stem: Which two inputs does a text-to-speech (speech synthesis) solution need at minimum?
options: An audio file and a language model
The text to speak and the voice to use
A transcript and a SAS URI
questions.explain: Speech synthesis needs the text and a voice. Audio files and SAS URIs are inputs to speech recognition or batch transcription, and images relate to vision.

questions.stem: Complete the code to speak a plain-text message through the default speaker.
questions.code:
speech_config.speech_synthesis_voice_name = "en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural"
audio_config = speechsdk.audio.AudioOutputConfig(use_default_speaker=True)
synth = speechsdk.SpeechSynthesizer(speech_config=speech_config, audio_config=audio_config)
result = synth.____("Your order has shipped.").get()
questions.explain: speak_text_async synthesises plain text. speak_ssml_async expects an SSML XML document, and the recognition methods convert speech to text rather than text to speech.

questions.stem: For each statement about speech synthesis, select Yes if it is true. Otherwise, select No.

statements.s: SSML is a JSON format for specifying voice settings.
SSML can insert pauses and adjust speaking rate and pitch.
Neural voices use deep neural networks to produce more natural intonation than older synthetic voices.

questions.explain: SSML is XML-based, not JSON. It controls breaks, prosody (rate, pitch, volume), pronunciation and styles. Neural voices give more natural-sounding speech.

questions.case: An airline's announcement app reads flight notices aloud with a neural voice. Product owners want a half-second pause after the flight number and a slightly slower rate for gate changes. The developer currently calls speak_text_async with plain strings.
questions.stem: What should the developer do?
options: Raise the model temperature for the voice
Build an SSML document with break and prosody elements and call speak_ssml_async
Add a stop sequence after the flight number
questions.explain: SSML's break and prosody rate elements control pauses and speed, and it's sent with speak_ssml_async. Temperature and stop sequences are LLM generation settings, and batch transcription is speech-to-text.

questions.stem: You want users to upload a photo and ask questions about what it shows. Which kind of model should you deploy in Microsoft Foundry?
options: A multimodal (vision-enabled) chat model such as gpt-4.1-mini
A text embedding model such as text-embedding-3-large
A speech-to-text model in Azure Speech in Foundry Tools
An image generation model such as GPT-image-1.5
questions.explain: A multimodal model accepts an image and text in one prompt and answers in natural language. Embedding models return vectors, not answers. GPT-image models create or edit images rather than answer questions about them. Speech-to-text transcribes audio.
